messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

Claims:
1. "The LIVR framework decomposes semantic features into different places by utilizing a segmentation map and extracting place-based feature descriptions individually." -- cites: E1 (Figure 2): quote "Given the segmentation map, we decompose the semantic features into different places and extract place-based feature descriptions individually, then dynamically aggregate them at inference time according to the topology of the scene."
2. "The framework dynamically aggregates the decomposed features at inference time according to the topology of the scene." -- cites: E1 (Figure 2): quote "Given the segmentation map, we decompose the semantic features into different places and extract place-based feature descriptions individually, then dynamically aggregate them at inference time according to the topology of the scene."
3. "The LIVR framework employs a segmentation map to decompose features and extract place-based feature descriptions individually." -- cites: E3 (Section 3.2): quote "Segmentation Maps Semantic Feature Decomposition utilizes a segmentation map of each place to decompose features and cause the network to extract place-based feature descriptions individually."

Cited evidence:

Given the segmentation map, we decompose the semantic features into different places and extract place-based feature descriptions individually, then dynamically aggregate them at inference time according to the topology of the scene. ⊙ denotes the masking operation for spatial decomposition. "NN" stands for neural network.

[E3] (text, Section 3.2, page 3): Segmentation Maps Semantic Feature Decomposition utilizes a segmentation map of each place to decompose features and cause the network to extract place-based feature descriptions individually. The segmentation maps can be manually constructed using a mobile app we developed 2 to annotate each place by drawing points to construct polygons. This is reasonable since most smart home customers have only one or two cameras in their home. We employ human annotations because automatic semantic segmentation methods segment places based on appearance ( e.g., color, texture, etc. ), while our task requires differentiation between places with similar appearance based on function- [image]
